summary: This article explains how the Nile forms from two branches, flows north through the desert, once flooded every year to leave rich soil, builds a delta, and changed after the Aswan High Dam.
introduce: Read the title “The Nile: A River of Life” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: one of the parts that join together to make a bigger river
able to grow many healthy plants

challengeTerms.def: a smaller river or stream that flows into a bigger river
sand, mud, and tiny bits of rock carried by water and left in a new place
bringing water to fields through pipes or canals so crops can grow

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that stopping the Nile's yearly flood was a good idea? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain one good result and one problem that came from the Aswan High Dam.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review branch, current, and fertile, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use tributary, sediment, and irrigation in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
